rationale: B wins by a nose because it gives the founder sharper editorial doors, especially "Schools are getting AI student tutors. Teachers are quietly getting something else: an AI lesson planner." That is a real workforce angle, not just rollout wallpaper. A has strong discipline, but "A nonprofit is giving an AI tutor to teachers for free while the rest of ed-tech charges per seat" smuggles an unsupported market claim into the headline. B still needs a fact sweep; it is better architecture, not clean copy.
gaps_in_A: "A nonprofit is giving an AI tutor to teachers for free while the rest of ed-tech charges per seat" asserts a category-wide pricing contrast not in the facts; the update only says Khanmigo is free to teachers and donor-funded.
"one of the largest AI-tutoring deployments" is an unproven superlative. The 1 million additional students figure is real; the ranking is not supplied.

"Khanmigo lands in 30 more districts — what changes inside the classrooms that get it" is serviceable but soft. It does not separate student tutoring from teacher lesson-planning sharply enough, so it risks becoming rollout color.

"thoughtful education or policy outlet" is a little foggy compared with the stronger sub-beats elsewhere. Name the actual lane: learning science, education psychology, K-12 policy, or ed-tech accountability.
gaps_in_B: "districts are signing on to expand to 1 million students based on a study" invents motivation. The update says the study and rollout are being announced together, not that districts relied on the study.
"a body of research on productive failure and desirable difficulty" imports outside research not in the update. Fine as proof to go find; not fine as a stated premise in a blind angle set.
"While VC-backed EdTech companies charge districts" is an unsupported category contrast. The facts do not mention competitors, VC-backed companies, or district pricing.
"public school teachers" is a small but avoidable assumption. The update says US school districts and teachers; keep the wording there unless the public-school status is confirmed.
